nodes.summary: For a binary Boolean operation $\mathrm{op}$ and binary decision diagrams $t_1, t_2$, the diagram $A_{\mathrm{op}}(t_1, t_2)$ is defined by recursion. If $t_1$ and $t_2$ are leaves with values $a$ and $b$, it is the leaf with value $\mathrm{op}(a, b)$. Otherwise let $v$ be the smallest variable tested at the root of $t_1$ or of $t_2$ (a leaf tests none), and for $i = 1, 2$ let $\ell_i$ and $h_i$ be the low and high…
nodes.title: Bryant's apply operation

nodes.summary: A binary decision diagram, in tree form, is either a leaf carrying a Boolean value, or a node consisting of a variable $v \in \mathbb{N}$ and two diagrams: the low child, for $v$ false, and the high child, for $v$ true.
nodes.title: Binary decision diagram

nodes.summary: If $t_1$ and $t_2$ are reduced ordered binary decision diagrams, then $t_1 = t_2$ if and only if $t_1$ and $t_2$ have the same value under every assignment of Boolean values to the variables.
nodes.title: Reduced ordered diagrams are equal iff they have the same values

nodes.summary: A reduced ordered binary decision diagram $t$ is the leaf with value false if and only if $t$ has value false under every assignment of Boolean values to the variables.
nodes.title: Unsatisfiable reduced ordered diagrams

nodes.summary: Canonicity (Bryant): two reduced ordered diagrams with the same function are equal.
nodes.title: Canonicity

nodes.summary: For every binary Boolean operation $\mathrm{op}$, all binary decision diagrams $t_1$ and $t_2$, and every assignment $\sigma$ of Boolean values to the variables, the value under $\sigma$ of the diagram $\mathrm{apply}(\mathrm{op}, t_1, t_2)$ obtained from $t_1$ and $t_2$ by Bryant's apply operation under $\mathrm{op}$ is $\mathrm{op}(a_1, a_2)$, where $a_i$ is the value of $t_i$ under $\sigma$.
nodes.title: Apply computes the operation pointwise

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a node testing the variable $v$ with low child $\ell$ and high child $h$, and suppose $t$ is ordered from some $n \in \mathbb{N}$. For every assignment $\sigma$ of Boolean values to the variables and every Boolean $b$, the value of $t$ under $\sigma[v \mapsto b]$ (the assignment $\sigma$ with $v$ set to $b$) is the value of $h$ under $\sigma$ if $b$ is true, and the value of $\ell$ under $\sigma$ if $b$…
nodes.title: Fixing the top variable of an ordered node

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a binary decision diagram ordered from $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $v < n$ be a variable. For every assignment $\sigma$ of Boolean values to the variables and every Boolean $b$, the value of $t$ under $\sigma[v \mapsto b]$ (the assignment $\sigma$ with $v$ set to $b$) equals the value of $t$ under $\sigma$.
nodes.title: Independence from variables below the order

nodes.summary: Under an assignment $\sigma$ of a Boolean value to each variable $v \in \mathbb{N}$, the value of a leaf is its Boolean value, and the value of a node testing $v$ is the value of its high child if $\sigma(v)$ is true and the value of its low child if $\sigma(v)$ is false.
nodes.title: Evaluation of a binary decision diagram

nodes.summary: A binary decision diagram is a reduced ordered binary decision diagram (ROBDD), for the natural order on variables, when it is ordered from $0$ (the tested variables strictly increase along every path) and reduced (no node has two equal children).
nodes.title: Reduced ordered binary decision diagram

nodes.summary: For a variable $v \in \mathbb{N}$ and diagrams $\ell$ and $h$, the diagram $\mathrm{mk}(v, \ell, h)$ is $\ell$ if $\ell = h$, and otherwise the node that tests $v$ with $\ell$ as its false-child and $h$ as its true-child.
nodes.title: Node constructor removing a redundant test

nodes.summary: For propositions $A$ and $B$ over natural-number atoms, the binary decision diagrams of $A$ and $B$ are equal if and only if $A$ and $B$ have the same truth value under every valuation $\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$.
nodes.title: Equal BDDs iff equal truth tables

nodes.summary: For a proposition $A$ over natural-number atoms, the binary decision diagram of $A$ is not the leaf false if and only if some valuation $\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ makes $A$ true.
nodes.title: Satisfiable iff the BDD is not the false leaf

nodes.summary: Each proposition $A$ whose atoms are natural numbers is sent to a binary decision diagram by recursion on $A$: an atom $x$ goes to the node testing $x$ with the leaf false as its false-child and the leaf true as its true-child, and a conjunction $A \wedge B$, disjunction $A \vee B$ or implication $A \to B$ goes to the result of apply on the diagrams of $A$ and $B$ under the Boolean operation and, or, or…
nodes.title: Diagram of a proposition

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{op}$ be a binary Boolean operation and $n$ a natural number. If the diagrams $t_1$ and $t_2$ are both ordered from $n$, then the result of apply with $\mathrm{op}$ on $t_1$ and $t_2$ is ordered from $n$.
nodes.title: Apply preserves orderedness

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, a diagram is ordered from $n$ when every variable it tests is at least $n$ and the tested variables strictly increase along every path. Recursively: every leaf is ordered from $n$, and the node testing $v$ with children $\ell$ and $h$ is ordered from $n$ when $n \le v$ and both $\ell$ and $h$ are ordered from $v + 1$.
nodes.title: Diagrams ordered from a variable

nodes.summary: For every binary Boolean operation $\mathrm{op}$ and all diagrams $t_1$ and $t_2$, the result of apply with $\mathrm{op}$ on $t_1$ and $t_2$ is reduced.
nodes.title: Apply returns reduced diagrams

nodes.summary: A diagram is reduced when no node in it has two equal children: every leaf is reduced, and the node testing $v$ with children $\ell$ and $h$ is reduced when $\ell \ne h$ and both $\ell$ and $h$ are reduced.
nodes.title: Reduced diagrams

nodes.summary: For every binary decision diagram $t$, the size of $t$ (its number of leaves and nodes, counted in tree form) is strictly positive.
nodes.title: Binary decision diagrams have positive size

nodes.summary: The size of a diagram is its number of leaves and nodes, counted in tree form: a leaf has size $1$, and a node with children $\ell$ and $h$ has size one more than the sum of the sizes of $\ell$ and $h$.
nodes.title: Size of a diagram

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
